variants.title: Move a change through the pipeline
variants.context: The pipeline is a sequence of increasingly expensive decisions: declare the change, run targeted evidence, apply the release gates, grant bounded exposure, join live outcomes, then contain and learn.
variants.prompt: A prompt change is ready and the team wants to ship it to all users this afternoon. Put the pipeline stages in order.

items.text: Join live traces to quality, safety, latency, cost, and delayed task outcomes by release identity.
Start in shadow or a small canary with abort criteria and a last known-good rollback target.
Record the candidate model, prompt, retrieval snapshot, tool versions, and the product claims this change touches.
Run deterministic checks, changed-path regressions, product cases, critical slices, and calibrated judgment.
Pause or roll back a failing route, preserve the incident evidence, and add the failure to a future regression set.
Compare against the frozen baseline using uncertainty bounds, hard safety limits, and slice floors.

variants.hint: Cheap deterministic failures should stop the change before expensive evidence runs.
variants.explanation: Passing offline evidence buys bounded exposure. Production outcomes, joined to release identity, are what justify widening it.

variants.title: Move a change through the pipeline
variants.context: The pipeline is a sequence of increasingly expensive decisions: declare the change, run targeted evidence, apply the release gates, grant bounded exposure, join live outcomes, then contain and learn.
variants.prompt: A retrieval index is being upgraded, and last quarter a similar change regressed one language without anyone noticing. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Attribute live quality and citation metrics to the index version and language cohort.
Run the changed-path regressions and per-language product cases against the new snapshot.
Route a small share of traffic to the new index while keeping the old snapshot warm as the rollback target.
Roll back the affected route and promote the confirmed failure into a new regression-set version.
Declare the new index snapshot as the candidate and name the grounded-answer claims it affects.
Read the per-language floors and the uncertainty-aware comparison with the previous snapshot.

variants.hint: Which stage makes the language cohort visible in live traffic?
variants.explanation: Identity recorded at the start is what lets production signals be joined to the candidate path at the end.

variants.title: Move a change through the pipeline
variants.context: The pipeline is a sequence of increasingly expensive decisions: declare the change, run targeted evidence, apply the release gates, grant bounded exposure, join live outcomes, then contain and learn.
variants.prompt: A model provider deprecates the current version and a replacement must ship within the week. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Execute the frozen portfolio against the replacement, including the safety and critical-slice suites.
Watch cohort-level quality, latency, and cost joined to the new release identity.
Apply the predeclared regression tolerance and hard blockers rather than accepting a schedule-driven exception.
Register the replacement model, its decoding settings, and every claim the current model supports.
Expose the replacement behind a flag at a small percentage with abort thresholds attached.
Keep the old route available until the canary evidence supports widening, and record the decision either way.

variants.hint: A deadline changes the schedule, not the order of the evidence.
variants.explanation: The gate order is fixed so that time pressure produces a recorded exception rather than a skipped stage.

variants.title: Triage a production signal
variants.context: Production monitoring counts as evaluation only when a signal can be attributed to a release path. Triage moves from the broad signal to causal evidence before anyone changes the product.
variants.prompt: A dashboard shows fleet quality dropping four points overnight and someone proposes rolling back the model immediately. Put the triage steps in order.

items.text: Slice by candidate assignment, task, language, tenant, and time window to find where the drop lives.
Join versioned traces to identify the first component that differs between healthy and failing requests.
Check event definitions, missing data, delays, and duplicate events before assuming behavior changed.
Contain according to risk, rolling back only the route where a bounded failure is attributable.
Retain the cases, traces, raw outputs, and decision record, then add the validated failure to a new regression version.

variants.hint: A dashboard movement can start before any model behavior does.
variants.explanation: Instrumentation is validated first because a broken join or a duplicated event can imitate a severe regression.

variants.title: Triage a production signal
variants.context: Production monitoring counts as evaluation only when a signal can be attributed to a release path. Triage moves from the broad signal to causal evidence before anyone changes the product.
variants.prompt: Quality looks flat overall, but a support team reports that Spanish answers got worse after a retrieval change. Put the triage steps in order.

items.text: Preserve the failing traces and promote them into the next version of the regression set.
Confirm the Spanish outcome events are still being recorded and joined at the same rate as before.
Compare the Spanish cohort against an equivalent control cohort on the previous retrieval route.
Route Spanish traffic back to the previous index while leaving healthy cohorts on the new one.
Trace a sample of failing Spanish requests to the first component whose version differs from the control.

variants.hint: A flat fleet average is not evidence that every cohort is flat.
variants.explanation: Comparing equivalent cohorts is what separates a real slice regression from a shift in the traffic mix.

variants.title: Triage a production signal
variants.context: Production monitoring counts as evaluation only when a signal can be attributed to a release path. Triage moves from the broad signal to causal evidence before anyone changes the product.
variants.prompt: Safety failures appear to double, and an instrumentation release also shipped in the same window. Put the triage steps in order.

items.text: Pause expansion while the attribution is uncertain rather than rolling back an unproven cause.
Compare cohorts that ran on identical instrumentation to see whether the increase survives.
Verify whether the safety event definition changed or whether the same events are now counted twice.
Store the incident evidence and the decision, including what the team could not yet attribute.
Join traces by release and policy version to locate the first differing component on the failing path.

variants.hint: Two changes shipped together, and only one of them touches the model.
variants.explanation: Pause is the correct containment when a failure is real but not yet attributable to the candidate path.

variants.title: Compute the delta in percentage points
variants.context: A release gate compares candidate and baseline as rates, not as raw counts. The delta is stated in percentage points so the same tolerance can be read across suites of different sizes.
variants.prompt: On a critical slice the baseline passes 152 of 200 cases and the candidate passes 137 of 200. Higher is better. How many percentage points is the candidate below the baseline?
variants.hint: Convert each count to a rate before comparing them.
variants.explanation: The gate reads a difference of rates in percentage points, which keeps one tolerance readable across suites of different sizes.

mistakes.feedback: You subtracted the counts, 152 minus 137, instead of the rates.
That is the difference as a proportion; the gate is written in percentage points.

variants.title: Compute the delta in percentage points
variants.context: A release gate compares candidate and baseline as rates, not as raw counts. The delta is stated in percentage points so the same tolerance can be read across suites of different sizes.
variants.prompt: On the answer-quality suite the baseline passes 780 of 1000 cases and the candidate passes 815 of 1000. Higher is better. How many percentage points is the candidate above the baseline?
variants.hint: Turn both results into rates first, then take the difference.
variants.explanation: A point delta is only the starting number; the gate still reads the conservative bound before promoting the candidate.

mistakes.feedback: You subtracted the counts instead of the rates.
That is the proportional difference, not percentage points.

variants.title: Compute the delta in percentage points
variants.context: A release gate compares candidate and baseline as rates, not as raw counts. The delta is stated in percentage points so the same tolerance can be read across suites of different sizes.
variants.prompt: A safety suite grew between runs. The baseline passes 776 of 800 cases and the candidate passes 470 of 500. Higher is better. How many percentage points is the candidate below the baseline?
variants.hint: The two runs do not share a denominator, so the counts cannot be compared directly.
variants.explanation: Rates make runs with different sample sizes comparable, which is why the gate is written on rates rather than counts.

mistakes.feedback: You subtracted the counts, which are not comparable across different denominators.
That is the proportional difference, not percentage points.

variants.title: Choose evidence for the question
variants.context: Different questions need different evidence. Deterministic checks establish exact properties, calibrated judges apply a rubric at scale, human reviewers resolve nuanced cases, and product outcomes show whether the real task was completed.
variants.prompt: A pull request must prove that every tool call still returns the declared schema and that no call writes outside its sandbox.
options: Run a deterministic contract and side-effect check on every tool call in the smoke set.
Ask a calibrated judge to rate whether each tool response looks well formed and safe.
Sample the changed tool calls for review by a trained human reviewer before merge.
optionFeedback: Schema validity and side effects are exact properties, so a deterministic check settles them.
A judge estimates a rubric when an exact check already exists and runs far cheaper.
Human review is expensive judgment spent on a property a test can decide outright.
variants.hint: Can this property be executed and compared exactly?
variants.explanation: Deterministic checks establish exact properties such as schema validity, executable tests, and tool side effects.

variants.title: Choose evidence for the question
variants.context: Different questions need different evidence. Deterministic checks establish exact properties, calibrated judges apply a rubric at scale, human reviewers resolve nuanced cases, and product outcomes show whether the real task was completed.
variants.prompt: A team must rate rubric adherence across 40,000 open-ended answers each week, with a weekly release deadline.
options: Apply a versioned judge with blind position swaps, measured agreement, and sampled disagreements.
Replace the rubric with a keyword check so the whole population can be scored deterministically.
Send a random 5 percent to human reviewers and extrapolate the rubric score to the rest.
optionFeedback: A calibrated judge applies the rubric at scale while its agreement and bias stay measured.
A keyword proxy is exact about the wrong property and silently drops the rubric being claimed.
Extrapolating from a small sample reports one number without measuring how well it generalizes.
variants.hint: Which option keeps both the scale and a measurement of its own reliability?
variants.explanation: Model judges scale a rubric, but only with position swaps, agreement measurement, and versioned judge prompts.

variants.title: Choose evidence for the question
variants.context: Different questions need different evidence. Deterministic checks establish exact properties, calibrated judges apply a rubric at scale, human reviewers resolve nuanced cases, and product outcomes show whether the real task was completed.
variants.prompt: Task-completion telemetry arrives days late, mixes cohorts, and is collected only from users who returned to the product.
options: Drop product outcomes from the pipeline, since delay and selection make them unreliable.
Join the outcomes to release and cohort identity, and read them beside offline evidence.
Treat the completion metric as the primary release gate once enough days have passed.
optionFeedback: Product outcomes are the only signal about the real task, so discarding them removes the point of monitoring.
Joining to release and cohort identity is what makes a confounded outcome interpretable.
Promoting a delayed and selection-biased metric to primary gate hides who was actually measured.
variants.hint: What has to be true before a delayed metric can be attributed to anything?
variants.explanation: Product outcomes reveal whether users completed the real task, but they must be joined with release and cohort identity.

variants.title: Preserve the four identities
variants.context: Every result carries four identities: release identity says what shipped, evidence identity says what it was measured on, judgment identity says how it was scored, and decision identity says what the score authorized.
variants.prompt: A stored pipeline result lists four groups of fields. Match each group to the identity it records.

pairs.label: Release identity
pairs.detail: Candidate and baseline model, prompt, policy, retrieval, tool, and feature-flag versions.

pairs.label: Evidence identity
pairs.detail: Dataset and split version, case IDs, cohort labels, and contamination status.

pairs.label: Judgment identity
pairs.detail: Checker or judge version, rubric, judge prompt, and the human-review agreement result.

pairs.label: Decision identity
pairs.detail: Thresholds, uncertainty method, exposure percentage, owner, and rollback target.

variants.hint: Ask whether the field describes what shipped, what it was measured on, how it was scored, or what it authorized.
variants.explanation: A promotion decision must be reproducible from these four together; any missing one breaks the comparison.

variants.title: Preserve the four identities
variants.context: Every result carries four identities: release identity says what shipped, evidence identity says what it was measured on, judgment identity says how it was scored, and decision identity says what the score authorized.
variants.prompt: Four fields were left out of a release record and the comparison is now disputed. Match each missing field to its identity.

pairs.label: Release identity
pairs.detail: The feature flag that routed this cohort to the candidate.

pairs.label: Evidence identity
pairs.detail: The sampling policy that selected the cases scored in this run.

pairs.label: Judgment identity
pairs.detail: The rubric version the reviewers applied to disagreements.

pairs.label: Decision identity
pairs.detail: The approved exception that let the rollout continue.

variants.hint: A sampling policy describes the cases, not the scoring of them.
variants.explanation: The workflow fails closed on mutable or missing identities, because an unrecorded change makes the comparison invalid.

variants.title: Preserve the four identities
variants.context: Every result carries four identities: release identity says what shipped, evidence identity says what it was measured on, judgment identity says how it was scored, and decision identity says what the score authorized.
variants.prompt: A post-incident review asks four questions. Match each question to the identity that answers it.

pairs.label: Release identity
pairs.detail: Which retrieval snapshot were these requests served from?

pairs.label: Evidence identity
pairs.detail: Which cases and cohort labels produced the offline score?

pairs.label: Judgment identity
pairs.detail: Which judge prompt decided that these answers passed?

pairs.label: Decision identity
pairs.detail: Who approved this exposure level and what was the abort rule?

variants.hint: One of these questions is about accountability rather than measurement.
variants.explanation: A healthy pipeline makes one decision legible: what changed, what ran, what passed, who approved it, and how to get back.
